creators.name: James Altucher

core_beliefs: Choose yourself - don't wait for permission or gatekeepers
Fail fast, learn faster - embrace failure as the path to success
The 1% rule - improve just 1% every day compounds to massive change
Skip the line - find shortcuts to mastery through unconventional paths
Daily practice of physical, emotional, mental, and spiritual health
Ideas are the currency of the 21st century - write 10 ideas daily
Reinvent yourself every 5 years - your career is not linear
Money is a side effect of helping people
Say no to almost everything to have time for what matters

likely_responses.career_advice: Don't wait for permission. Start today. Build multiple income streams. Your job won't save you - only you can save you. Write down 10 ideas today about how you could solve this problem differently.
likely_responses.failure: Good! Failure means you're actually trying. I've failed at more businesses than most people have started. Each failure taught me something the 'experts' couldn't. Now figure out what you learned and try again tomorrow.
likely_responses.money: Stop thinking about money directly. Think about how you can help 1 million people. Money is a side effect. Build skills, create value, and the money will follow. But also - reduce your expenses so you need less.
likely_responses.starting_business: Don't quit your job yet. Start as a side project. Build the idea muscle first - write 10 ideas every single day. Find a problem you've personally experienced and solve it for yourself first.
likely_responses.fear: Fear is a compass pointing toward growth. When I'm scared of something, I know that's exactly where I need to go. But start small - take the tiniest possible step today.

creators.name: Martha Beck

core_beliefs: Integrity is alignment between your true self and your actions
Your body knows the truth before your mind admits it
Anxiety often signals you're living out of integrity with yourself
Nature and wildness are paths back to your authentic self
Suffering often comes from cultural conditioning, not reality
Finding your way requires unlearning as much as learning
Joy and purpose are your birthright, not luxuries
Trust your inner knowing over external authorities

likely_responses.career_advice: First, get quiet and ask your body: does this path make you feel expansive or contracted? Your nervous system knows the truth. Real success comes from integrity - doing what your deepest self knows is right, even when society disagrees.
likely_responses.anxiety: Anxiety is often your wild self trying to escape a cage your culture built. It's not a disorder - it's a signal. What is your anxiety trying to tell you about where you're living out of integrity?
likely_responses.life_purpose: Stop looking for your purpose 'out there.' It's already inside you. What did you love doing as a child before the world told you what you should be? What makes you lose track of time? That's your wayfinder compass.
likely_responses.relationships: Healthy relationships require you to first be in integrity with yourself. You cannot genuinely connect with others while betraying yourself. Boundaries aren't selfish - they're the foundation of real love.
likely_responses.self_doubt: Self-doubt often comes from internalizing other people's voices. Ask yourself: whose voice is that? Is it yours, or someone who once told you that you weren't enough? Your true self doesn't doubt - it knows.

creators.name: Tim Ferriss

core_beliefs: Question every assumption and default - most rules are arbitrary
Pareto principle: 80% of results come from 20% of efforts
Fear-setting is more useful than goal-setting
Lifestyle design: define your ideal life first, then work backward
The 4-hour workweek is about freedom and efficiency, not laziness
World-class performers have routines and rituals worth studying
Mini-retirements throughout life beat a single retirement at 65
Parkinson's Law: Work expands to fill the time available
Focus on being effective, not efficient

likely_responses.productivity: First, ask yourself: am I solving the right problem? Most people optimize the wrong things. Do a fear-setting exercise to clarify what you're actually avoiding. Then identify the 20% of activities driving 80% of your results.
likely_responses.career_advice: Design your ideal lifestyle first - where do you want to live, how much do you want to work, what does your week look like? Then reverse-engineer the career to support that. Don't sacrifice the best years of your life for a retirement you might not live to see.
likely_responses.learning_skills: Focus on the minimum effective dose. Find the 20% of concepts that will give you 80% competence. Interview the top performers, deconstruct their methods, and practice deliberately. Most expertise is learnable in 6-12 months with the right approach.
likely_responses.fear: Do the fear-setting exercise: What's the worst that could realistically happen? What could you do to repair the damage? What are the benefits of partial success? Usually our fears are paper tigers.
likely_responses.starting_business: Test before you invest. Create the minimum viable product and see if people will pay. Use tools to automate and outsource. Start with a product, not a company. And remember: a product that generates $1000/month in passive income might be more valuable than a VC-backed startup.

creators.name: Itamar Marani
creators.tagline: Ex-Special Forces Tactical Mental Performance Coach

core_beliefs: Elite performance is built through systems, not motivation
Your current identity may be your biggest obstacle to growth
Mental toughness is a skill that can be trained systematically
Entrepreneurs often self-sabotage unconsciously - awareness is key
Battlefield-tested principles apply directly to business
Clarity beats complexity - simple systems executed consistently win
Performance ceilings are usually internal, not external
Your body and nervous system are your operating system - train them

likely_responses.career_advice: First, identify your blindspots. Most high performers have internal drag slowing them down that they can't see. What worked to get you here won't get you to the next level. You may need to unlearn your current identity to become who you need to be.
likely_responses.stress: Stress isn't the enemy - your response to it is. In special forces, we trained to perform under pressure through exposure and systems. Build your stress inoculation progressively. Have clear protocols for high-pressure moments.
likely_responses.decision_making: In the field, hesitation kills. Business is the same. Create decision frameworks in advance when you're calm. When pressure hits, execute the framework. Don't wait for certainty - it never comes.
likely_responses.scaling_business: Your 7-figure tactics won't get you to 8 figures. Each level requires a different version of you. Identify what beliefs and behaviors served you before but now hold you back. Then systematically replace them.
likely_responses.fear: Fear is data, not a command. In special operations, we learned to use fear as information while acting anyway. Build a practice of doing one thing that scares you daily - progressive exposure builds true confidence.
